land.text: Western Samoa: 'the two large islands of Upolu and Savai'i' and 'two smaller, inhabited islands (Manono and Apolima)'

predecessors.note: New Zealand 'officially gained control of the region as a League of Nations mandate in 1920' and held it 'as a Class C Mandate under trusteeship'; 'the New Zealand Western Samoa Act of 24 November 1961 terminated the Trusteeship Agreement'. The new-zealand dossier (oc-02-a) records the 1920 gain from german-samoa and the 1962 loss to samoa.

capitals.name: Apia
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Apia, '13°50′00″S 171°45′44″W'; the page says 'The capital and largest city is Apia.' No earlier or later seat is recorded.

correction.text: the independent state: Upolu and Savai'i with Manono and Apolima and the islets of the Apolima Strait and the Aleipata group; American Samoa, 64 km to the east, is a separate territory

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The country Samoa is cells: 9 (about 2276 km2); the page gives three areas without reconciling them (infobox 2,831 km2; geography 2,842 km2; economy 2,934 km2). Against 2,831 the grid is about 0.8 of the land (the small islands do not fill a cell). 'Samoa is located 64 km west of American Samoa'; American Samoa is not in this shape.

region.text: the Independent State of Western Samoa: Upolu, Savai'i, Manono and Apolima

ledger.note: 1962: Western Samoa becomes independent: 'Western Samoa gained independence on 1 January 1962'; the page says the New Zealand Western Samoa Act of 24 November 1961 'terminated the Trusteeship Agreement' and 'granted the country independence as the Independent State of Western Samoa, effective 1 January 1962'.

1997: Western Samoa becomes Samoa: 'On 4 July 1997, the government amended the constitution to change the name of the country from Western Samoa to Samoa'. American Samoa 'protested against the name change'. No land changes.

certainty.note: An island group; the border is the coast. The nearest neighbour, American Samoa, is 64 km east across open sea.

sources.title: Samoa
sources.note: Independence 1 January 1962 (Western Samoa Act of 24 November 1961), name change 4 July 1997, UN admission 15 December 1976, capital Apia with coordinates, area figures 2,831/2,842/2,934 km2, islands, American Samoa 64 km east.

notes: Written by oc-02-x. One page opened (Samoa, fetched in three questions). Cliopatria has no row for Samoa after 1900; the land 1900-1920 is german-samoa (this batch) and 1920-1962 is New Zealand's (oc-02-a). The independence date is the one the page gives twice (1 January 1962). The page says Western Samoa was admitted to the United Nations on 15 December 1976 (not a border event). It gives three land areas (2,831, 2,842 and 2,934 km2) and does not say in so many words that American Samoa is not part of the country; the 64 km figure and the history of the eastern islands as a US territory are what the dossier rests on. American Samoa has no dossier from this batch (the US row draws no cell for it).
